newsitem.title: CHINA: China actual jobless rate 4.5 pct - statistician.
newsitem.headline: China actual jobless rate 4.5 pct - statistician.

text.p: China's actual unemployment rate would be about 4.5 percent if the number of employees of state firms that have stopped or cut production were included in the figures, a government statistician said on Friday.

The government has given its urban unemployment rate as 3.0 percent, or about 5.3 million people, by end-1996 and by end-March. The figure consisted only of urban workers who are jobless and have asked the government to help them find work.
"Three percent...is (a figure) acceptable to society," State Statistical Bureau chief economist Qiu Xiaohua told reporters.
If the 7.5 million employees of state enterprises that have stopped or cut production were included, China's actual unemployment rate would be about 4.5 percent, Qiu said.
China has about 15 million surplus workers, who still do not count as unemployed, he said.
"Resolving the unemployment problem is one of China's long-term economic problems...We cannot ease off at any time," Qiu said.
The government has launched a programme to help the jobless to find work and was confident it would be able to rein in the figure to within four percent, he said.
Qiu defended the unemployment figure, saying many urban residents are jobless because they refuse to do what they see as menial work, such as collecting nightsoil from public toilets.
